extensionDescription.message: See a message sender's HubSpot record and log messages to their timeline.

panel_no_open_message.message: Open a message to see HubSpot details.

panel_you_sent_note.message: You sent this message — showing the recipient instead.

panel_never_log_note.message: This address is on your never-log list. Lookup and logging are disabled for it.

panel_log_already_logged.message: This message was already logged from this Thunderbird profile.

panel_log_never_log_blocked.message: Logging blocked because $EMAIL$ is on your never-log list.

panel_error_generic.message: HubSpot request failed. Check the Console for details.

panel_error_not_enabled.message: HubSpot access is turned off, so nothing has been sent. Turn it on in Settings to look up this sender in HubSpot.

panel_error_not_configured.message: Add your HubSpot access token in Settings to get started.

compose_no_recipients.message: Add a recipient to see HubSpot matches.

compose_bcc_already_present.message: Logging BCC is already on this message.

compose_bcc_never_log_blocked.message: Logging is blocked because $EMAIL$ is on your never-log list.

compose_no_bcc_configured.message: Set a logging BCC address in Settings to use this.

compose_error_not_enabled.message: HubSpot access is turned off, so nothing has been sent. Turn it on in Settings to look up these recipients in HubSpot.

compose_error_not_configured.message: Add your HubSpot access token in Settings to get started.

options_setup_intro.message: This add-on connects using a HubSpot access token, not a sign-in button. Here's why on the project page. HubSpot currently recommends creating a Service Key for integrations like this one; an existing private app token still works exactly the same way, so keep using it if you already have one.

options_credential_warning.message: Don't use a HubSpot “personal access key.” That's a different credential for the HubSpot CLI, limited to your own user permissions, and it isn't meant to be shared with an app like this one.

options_step1.message: New key: in HubSpot go to Development → Keys → Service keys → Create service key. Already have a private app? Settings → Integrations → Private Apps still works — use its token below instead.

options_step2.message: Add only the scopes below for the features you want, then finish creating the key.

options_step3.message: Copy the token into the field below and press Test connection.

options_scope_contacts_read_desc.message: Looking anyone up, and calls/meetings/notes in Recent activity — required

options_scope_sales_email_read_desc.message: Logging messages, and emails in Recent activity

options_token_label.message: HubSpot access token (Service Key or private app)

options_token_help.message: Works with either a Service Key or a private app access token — both use this same format. Stored locally in Thunderbird. Never sent anywhere except api.hubapi.com.

options_portal_id_help.message: Used to build "Open in HubSpot" links. Find it under Settings → Account Setup → Account Defaults.

options_bcc_help.message: Settings → Objects → Activities → Email Log & Track tab → Manual Logging → BCC Address → Copy. Lets the compose panel add it in one click.

options_never_log_help.message: One address or domain per line, e.g. person@example.com or example.com. These are never looked up or logged.

options_consent_intro.message: This add-on is turned off until you switch it on here. While it is on, it sends the following from this device to HubSpot's API at api.hubapi.com, over HTTPS:

options_consent_item_address.message: The email address, and display name if present, of the person whose message you are reading or composing — used to find their HubSpot contact record.

options_consent_item_message.message: The subject and body of a message, but only for the specific message you press “Log this message” on. Messages you merely read are never sent.

options_consent_item_token.message: Your HubSpot access token, as the authorization header on each request, so HubSpot knows the request is yours.

options_consent_when.message: Nothing is sent while this is off, and nothing is ever sent to the add-on's authors, to any analytics or telemetry service, or to any third party. HubSpot is the only destination this add-on can reach. Addresses on your never-log list are skipped even while it is on.

options_consent_checkbox_label.message: Allow this add-on to send the data described above to my HubSpot account

options_consent_help.message: You can switch this off at any time. Turning it off stops all outbound requests immediately and clears the in-memory lookup cache; your settings are kept.

options_consent_required_hint.message: Turn on “Send data to HubSpot” above before testing the connection.

options_test_success.message: Connected as $NAME$. Contact read access is working.

options_test_success_generic.message: Connected successfully. Contact read access is working.

options_privacy_note.message: No analytics, no telemetry, no third-party servers. All requests go straight from this device to api.hubapi.com, and only while the opt-in above is switched on.
